A dog kept howling but never got off the nail he was lying on.

Kevin Trudeau tells a story about a hound dog on a porch on a hot day. Every few minutes the dog lifted his head and howled, then lay back down. When Kevin asked why it didn't just move, his friend said the nail didn't hurt it that much.

Kevin's point: the pain wasn't bad enough to make the dog move, and people are exactly the same way.

What is your nail right now?

Dressing well is just as comfortable, says Kevin Trudeau.

Kevin describes a dinner in Las Vegas, all dressed up with his wife, surrounded by people in shorts, flip-flops and stained t-shirts. When someone said they were just comfortable, he pointed out that clothes that fit are every bit as comfortable.

His point: it isn't magic. Complacency is a choice, and anyone can put on nice clothes.

Where have you settled for the standard around you?

Arnold pinned photos of bodybuilders beside his bed.

Kevin Trudeau shares how a skinny young Arnold Schwarzenegger in Austria did this while his friends hung pictures of girls, and his mother worried. Every night he closed his eyes and saw himself on stage winning Mr. Olympia, with the trophy, the applause and the feeling.

Kevin says the picture Arnold held as a kid was almost identical to the real moment he won.

What picture do you hold in your mind at night?
